items.pronunciation_notes: Both vowels are short and the stress is even: pu-lis.

learn.explanation_en: पुलिस is borrowed from English and Hindi made it feminine — another arbitrary assignment, joining बस and मीटिंग against masculine बैंक. It is also treated as singular even though it refers to a force of many people: पुलिस आई, the police came, with a singular feminine verb. English does the opposite and treats police as plural, so both the gender and the number have to be unlearnt. Its verb is बुलाना, to call or summon.

examples.note: The तुम imperative — बुलाना is transitive.
Singular and feminine, where English would use a plural.
A compound borrowed whole, and worth having ready.

common_error.why_en: पुलिस is singular and feminine in Hindi, however many officers there are.

practice.question: पुलिस
practice.explanation_en: पुलिस is the police, feminine and singular in Hindi.

game.explanation_en: पुलिस बुलाना — to call or summon the police.

items.pronunciation_notes: The first syllable is very short and unstressed: pa-taa.

learn.title_en: मुझे पता है — one of the sentences you will use most
learn.explanation_en: पता is an address, masculine and Class 1. But it has a second life that matters far more: मुझे पता है means I know. Literally the knowledge is to me, with the person marked by को, exactly like मुझे भूख लगी है. And मुझे नहीं पता, I do not know, is the shortest useful sentence in the language. There is a separate verb जानना that also means to know, but for facts and information पता होना is what people actually say.

examples.note: The को construction — the knowledge belongs to me.
The auxiliary is dropped after नहीं, as usual.
The literal sense, with तुम्हारा agreeing with the masculine पता.

common_error.why_en: That sentence says you are an address. The knowledge is marked as belonging to you with को.

practice.prompt_en: What does मुझे पता है mean?
practice.question: मुझे पता है
practice.explanation_en: पता होना means to know. The same word is also the noun for an address.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with पता to mean knowing something?
game.explanation_en: पता होना — to know. पता लगाना means to find something out.

items.pronunciation_notes: Breathy bh at the front and a flapped ड़ at the end: bhiiṛ.

collocation.english: for there to be a crowd

learn.explanation_en: भीड़ is a crowd, feminine and flagged, and it is uncountable so it takes a singular verb: भीड़ है, not भीड़ हैं. This is the second word in this level where a group is grammatically singular, which is a general habit — Hindi treats collectives as one thing. भीड़ में means in the crowd, and बहुत भीड़ है is what you will say about almost any Indian market, station or road at almost any hour.

examples.note: Singular verb, since भीड़ is a collective.

examples.english: do not go into the crowd
examples.note: भीड़ is oblique before में, and मत negates the imperative.

examples.english: there was a crowd at the station
examples.note: थी is feminine singular, agreeing with भीड़.

common_error.why_en: भीड़ is one crowd however many people are in it, so the verb stays singular.

practice.question: भीड़
practice.explanation_en: भीड़ is a crowd, feminine, and grammatically singular.

game.explanation_en: भीड़ होना — a crowd exists. भीड़ लगना also occurs and means one gathers.

summary.recap_en: पुलिस and भीड़ are both collectives treated as grammatically singular, where English would use a plural for the first. पता is the most useful word in the level — मुझे पता है is how you say I know, and मुझे नहीं पता is the shortest useful sentence in Hindi.
summary.next_up_en: Next: electricity, queues and the temple — three fixtures of everyday Indian life.

items.pronunciation_notes: The middle vowel drops in speech, giving bij-lii rather than bi-ja-lii.

collocation.english: for the power to go out

learn.explanation_en: बिजली is electricity, feminine and predictable from its -ी. Its collocation is one you will need on your first day: बिजली चली गई, the power has gone. Hindi says the electricity went, using जाना, and बिजली आ गई for it coming back. Both verbs are intransitive, so the perfective is fully available. The same word also means lightning, which is where the electrical sense came from.

examples.note: Both verbs are feminine, agreeing with बिजली.
आना for its return, and गई again agrees with बिजली.
The plain statement, with नहीं in front of the verb.

common_error.why_en: बिजली is feminine, so both verbs take feminine forms. The -ी ending makes this one predictable.

practice.question: बिजली
practice.explanation_en: बिजली is electricity, and the same word also means lightning.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with बिजली when the power cuts out?
game.explanation_en: बिजली जाना — the electricity goes. बिजली आना is for it coming back.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two vowels running together with no consonant between: laa-in.

learn.title_en: लाइन में लगना — you attach yourself to the queue
learn.explanation_en: लाइन is borrowed from English and is feminine, like बस and मीटिंग. Its collocation is लाइन में लगना, to join a queue, using the same लगना that gave डर लगना and भूख लगना — here it means to attach or take a place. लगना is intransitive, so the perfective works: मैं लाइन में लगा, I joined the queue. The Hindi word क़तार also exists and is more formal.

examples.note: The तुम imperative — लगना is intransitive.
लंबी is feminine, which confirms लाइन is.

examples.english: there was a long queue at the bank
examples.note: थी is feminine singular, agreeing with लाइन.

common_error.why_en: लाइन is feminine in Hindi. English gives no gender at all, so this has to be memorised.

practice.question: लाइन
practice.explanation_en: लाइन is a queue, feminine, and it takes लगना for joining one.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with लाइन when you join one?
game.explanation_en: लाइन में लगना — the same लगना as भूख लगना, here meaning to take a place.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dot over म is an n before the द: man-dir.

learn.title_en: मंदिर, and the other places of worship
learn.explanation_en: मंदिर is a Hindu temple, masculine and Class 2. Hindi keeps a separate word for each faith's place of worship rather than a general term: मस्जिद for a mosque, which is feminine, गिरजाघर or चर्च for a church, and गुरुद्वारा for a gurdwara. मंदिर जाना takes no postposition like any destination. The word also appears figuratively, as in the idea of the body or the home as a मंदिर.

examples.note: The destination takes no postposition.
मंदिर is oblique before में, and भीड़ takes a singular verb.
पुराना is masculine, agreeing with मंदिर.

common_error.why_en: मंदिर is masculine. The consonant ending predicts nothing, hence the flag.

practice.question: मंदिर
practice.explanation_en: मंदिर is a Hindu temple. मस्जिद is a mosque, and it is feminine.

game.explanation_en: मंदिर जाना — and the destination takes no postposition.

summary.recap_en: बिजली जाना is the phrase you will use on your first day, and both it and बिजली आना are intransitive so every tense is open. लगना has now appeared with fear, hunger, injury and a queue — its common thread is attaching or taking hold.
summary.next_up_en: Next: government, the post office and cleanliness, closing the city block.

items.pronunciation_notes: The र is a light tap and the second syllable is long: sar-kaar.

learn.title_en: सरकार is feminine, and सरकारी is its adjective
learn.explanation_en: सरकार is the government, feminine and flagged. The adjective सरकारी, meaning governmental or state-run, is formed with the same -ी suffix that made दोस्ती and ख़ुशी — but here it produces an adjective rather than a noun, and it is unmarked so it never changes: सरकारी दफ़्तर, सरकारी नौकरी. That distinction is worth holding: the -ी suffix on an adjective gives an abstract noun, and on a noun it often gives a relational adjective.

examples.note: बदलना is intransitive, and गई is feminine, agreeing with सरकार.
सरकारी is unmarked and never changes.

examples.english: a government job is a good one
examples.note: अच्छी agrees with नौकरी; सरकारी does not change either way.

common_error.why_en: सरकारी has one form only. Working backwards from the -ी to invent a masculine is the same trap दुखी sets.

practice.question: सरकार
practice.explanation_en: सरकार is the government, feminine, and सरकारी is its adjective.

game.question_en: Which form describes a government office?
game.explanation_en: सरकारी दफ़्तर — the adjective is सरकारी and it never changes.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two words joined, with a breathy gh in the middle: ḍaak-ghar.

collocation.english: to go to the post office

learn.title_en: डाक plus घर — a compound you can read
learn.explanation_en: डाकघर is a post office, made of डाक, post or mail, and घर, house — so literally a mail-house. Hindi builds a lot of vocabulary this way and the gender comes from the second element, which is why डाकघर is masculine like घर. Once you notice that, compounds stop being intimidating: पुस्तकालय is a book-place, a library, and रसोईघर is a kitchen-house. The English पोस्ट ऑफ़िस is also widely used.

examples.note: The destination takes no postposition.
बंद is unmarked and never changes.
डाक on its own is feminine, which the compound does not inherit.

common_error.why_en: डाक alone is feminine but डाकघर takes its gender from घर, which is masculine. Compounds follow the last element.

practice.question: डाकघर
practice.explanation_en: डाकघर is a post office — डाक meaning mail plus घर meaning house.

game.question_en: Which element gives a Hindi compound its gender?
game.explanation_en: The last element. डाक is feminine but डाकघर is masculine, taking its gender from घर.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted फ़ is an f and the word ends on two vowels: sa-faa-ii.

learn.explanation_en: सफ़ाई is cleaning or cleanliness, formed from साफ़, clean, with the -आई suffix. That is the third time this suffix has appeared — पढ़ाई from पढ़ना, कमाई from कमाना — and everything it makes is feminine, so this gender needs no flag. सफ़ाई करना is to clean, and सफ़ाई कर्मचारी is a cleaner. The word also has a figurative sense of explaining yourself: सफ़ाई देना is to offer an excuse.

examples.note: The तुम imperative — करना is transitive.
The noun with होना, and नहीं in front of the verb.
साफ़ is the adjective, unmarked and never changing.

common_error.why_en: सफ़ाई is the noun cleanliness. To describe something as clean you need the adjective साफ़.

practice.question: सफ़ाई
practice.explanation_en: सफ़ाई is cleaning or cleanliness, formed from साफ़ with the -आई suffix.

game.explanation_en: सफ़ाई करना — cleaning is done, like पढ़ाई and मेहनत.

summary.recap_en: The city block is complete at twelve words. Compounds take their gender from the last element, which is why डाक is feminine and डाकघर masculine. The -ी suffix makes an abstract noun from an adjective but a relational adjective from a noun — दोस्ती against सरकारी.
summary.next_up_en: Next: time and the calendar, starting with dates and how often things happen.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ख़ at the end is made far back in the throat: taa-riikh.

learn.title_en: तारीख़ is a calendar date, not an appointment
learn.explanation_en: तारीख़ is the date on the calendar — the number, not a meeting you have arranged. आज क्या तारीख़ है asks what today's date is. It is feminine and flagged, with a dotted ख़ pronounced far back in the throat. The word also carries a second sense of history in more formal registers, which is where the Urdu-influenced तारीख़ी, historical, comes from.

examples.note: The standard way to ask, with क्या as the question word.
याद रखना from level twenty-six, for keeping something in mind.
की agrees with तारीख़, and तय होना means to be settled.

common_error.why_en: One date is singular, so है rather than हैं.

practice.question: तारीख़
practice.explanation_en: तारीख़ is the calendar date, feminine, and it also means history in formal use.

game.question_en: Which phrase goes with तारीख़ for keeping it in mind?
game.explanation_en: तारीख़ याद रखना — रखना for holding on to something deliberately.

items.pronunciation_notes: One long syllable with a rolled r: baar.

learn.explanation_en: बार is a time in the sense of an occasion, and it is how Hindi counts repetitions: एक बार once, दो बार twice, कई बार several times. It is feminine and flagged, and unusually it does not change in the plural — दो बार, not दो बारें. The doubled form बार-बार means again and again, and इस बार means this time. None of this overlaps with समय, which is time as a quantity rather than a count.

examples.note: Also used to mean just once, as a softener in requests.
बार does not change in the plural.
The doubled form means repeatedly, and मत negates the imperative.

common_error.why_en: बार is one of the few feminine nouns that does not take -ें in the plural when counting.

practice.question: एक बार
practice.explanation_en: बार counts occasions, so एक बार is once.

game.question_en: Which form means again and again?
game.explanation_en: बार-बार — doubling a word is a common way of intensifying it in Hindi.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ल्द cluster runs together with no vowel between: jal-dii.

learn.title_en: जल्दी covers quickly, soon and early
learn.explanation_en: जल्दी is an adverb meaning quickly, soon or early, and English needs three words where Hindi uses one: जल्दी आओ can be come quickly, come soon or come early depending on context. It never changes. It is also a feminine noun meaning hurry, which is where जल्दी करो, hurry up, comes from — literally do hurry. Its opposite is देर, which you met in the travel block and which behaves the same way.

examples.note: The noun sense — literally do hurry.
The adverb, describing how he comes.
The same word, now meaning quickly rather than early.

common_error.why_en: Hurrying is something you do, so करना. होना would say you are becoming hurry itself.

practice.question: जल्दी
practice.explanation_en: जल्दी is quickly, soon or early, and also the noun for hurry.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with जल्दी to mean hurry up?
game.explanation_en: जल्दी करो — hurrying is something you do.

summary.recap_en: बार counts occasions and does not change in the plural, which makes it unusual among feminine nouns. जल्दी covers quickly, soon and early in one word, and doubling — बार-बार — is a general way of intensifying in Hindi.
summary.next_up_en: Next: starting, always, and a conversation about being on time.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both syllables begin with a light consonant and the second is long: shu-ruu.

learn.explanation_en: शुरू means started or beginning, and it never changes. The two verbs split the same way they have all module: शुरू होना is for something beginning by itself — फ़िल्म शुरू हुई, the film started — while शुरू करना names the person doing the starting. Its opposite is ख़त्म, finished, which behaves identically: ख़त्म होना and ख़त्म करना. Both are unmarked, so neither will ever ask you for an ending.

examples.note: हुई is feminine, agreeing with क्लास.
करना names you as the one starting it.
The opposite, and फ़िल्म is feminine so गई agrees.

common_error.why_en: If the class simply began, होना is correct. करना would mean someone deliberately started it, and its perfective needs ने.

practice.question: शुरू
practice.explanation_en: शुरू means started or beginning. Its opposite is ख़त्म.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with शुरू when something begins by itself?
game.explanation_en: शुरू होना — it begins. करना names the person who starts it.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three syllables with the length on the last: ha-me-shaa.

learn.explanation_en: हमेशा means always, and like रोज़ it can only sit with the habitual — a thing that is always true cannot be described with the continuous. वह हमेशा देर से आता है, he is always late. That gives you a second reliable adverb test alongside रोज़ from Module 7. हमेशा never changes, and हमेशा के लिए means forever, which is the phrase to use for anything permanent.

examples.hindi: वह हमेशा देर से आता है
examples.read_as: vah hameshaa der se aataa hai
examples.note: हमेशा forces the habitual, exactly as रोज़ does.
जल्दी here means early, and उठना is intransitive.
The set phrase, using के लिए.

common_error.wrong: वह हमेशा देर से आ रहा है
common_error.right: वह हमेशा देर से आता है
common_error.why_en: हमेशा describes a standing fact, which the continuous cannot express. The habitual is the only option.

practice.question: हमेशा
practice.explanation_en: हमेशा is always, and like रोज़ it can only go with the habitual.

game.explanation_en: The habitual. A standing fact cannot be described with the continuous.

tts_strings: वह हमेशा देर से आता है

items.pronunciation_notes: The two words run together with the stress on होगी: shu-ruu ho-gii.

learn.title_en: Two adverbs, two tenses, one exchange
learn.explanation_en: The first two lines use the future, because the meeting has not started yet, and होगी is feminine because मीटिंग is. The second half switches to the habitual, because हमेशा forces it — you cannot describe an always with a continuous. So the exchange puts both of Module 7's adverb tests to work in four lines: हमेशा for the habitual, and a future for something not yet begun. Note जल्दी doing two jobs, meaning soon in the second line and early in the fourth.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: क्या तुम हमेशा देर से आते हो?
lines.read_as: kyaa tum hameshaa der se aate ho?

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: नहीं, मैं हमेशा जल्दी आता हूँ।
lines.read_as: nahiiṁ, maiṁ hameshaa jaldii aataa huuṁ.

common_error.why_en: मीटिंग is feminine in Hindi, so the verb is होगी. The English original gives no gender at all.

practice.question: जल्दी शुरू होगी
practice.explanation_en: The future of शुरू होना, with जल्दी meaning soon rather than early here.

game.question_en: Listen to the first line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: मीटिंग is feminine, so the future is होगी.

tts_strings: क्या तुम हमेशा देर से आते हो?
नहीं, मैं हमेशा जल्दी आता हूँ।

summary.recap_en: हमेशा joins रोज़ as an adverb that can only take the habitual, which gives you a second reliable test for choosing a tense. शुरू and ख़त्म both split होना for what happens by itself against करना for what someone does.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the rest of the time block, then adverbs of manner and frequency.
